row.reason: a row shard begins mid-column, so it carries an INITIAL_STATE plane, and the span-2 TCQ decoders this family's route packs for (tessera.lane_planes.pack_unit_for_kernel, csrc/window_gemv.cu) supply state_{-1} = 0 themselves; the loader refuses such a cut on EVERY rank, including rank 0 whose shard would pack, because a group whose ranks disagree about a module hangs on its first collective

tensor_parallel.units_note: max_world_size is an ATTESTATION bound: the largest tensor-parallel world size a served receipt covers. It is 1 for both families because no multi-rank serve has been run. loader_axes is a different claim -- what this build's LOADER does with each shard axis -- and it is checked against tessera.serving.sharding.ROUTE_TP_AXES, which the routes gate on, so the document and the code cannot drift. A serve above max_world_size is unattested, which is the same honest status a rung with no lane_eligibility cell has, and not a refusal.

changelog.change: tensor_parallel.units[] gains loader_axes: per axis, what this build's LOADER does with a shard on it ('sharded' or 'refused', plus a prose reason a gate does not read). The seam that cuts a unit landed (tessera.layout.slice_unit + serving/sharding), and the plugin's config gate had gone on refusing every tensor_parallel_size > 1 with a message saying the cutter was not in the build -- narrower than the code and, by then, false. The gate is now keyed on the slicer's PRESENCE, and the per-axis refusal moved to create_weights where the axis is known: TESSERA_E4M3_K1 cuts both axes (the window body's L-bit pad IS state_{-1}), TESSERA_E2M1_K2 cuts columns only (its span-2 TCQ decoders supply state_{-1} = 0 themselves). max_world_size is UNCHANGED at 1 and keeps its meaning -- the largest world size a served receipt covers -- because no multi-rank serve has been run; raising it needs a two-rank serve with a per-rank census and a KL against the single-rank arm, not a passing unit test. The validator no longer refuses a world size above one with the claim that a sharded form needs per-rank wires: it does not, the artifact is TP-agnostic and the cut happens at load. ADDITIVE -- a v1 reader that reads max_world_size still gets 1, which is the conservative answer.

reader_rate_range_q256 now states what the DECODER accepts, measured by encoding a unit at each candidate rate and running it through the route's own load path; the plugin refuses a declared q256 outside it (it did not before, and an allocated checkpoint carrying seven unlisted rungs served with nothing refusing). E4M3 widened from [1024,1024] to [256,2048] continuous at step 1 -- the bound is the trellis grammar's shaped domain (code rate 1..8 over an 8-bit-native alphabet), not the rungs anyone had exported. E2M1x2 stays the single point 896, bounded BELOW by the native decoder (span-2 TCQ only; the sub-cap WINDOW body has no served decode) and ABOVE by the same grammar (rate 7 of arity-2 native 8). candidate_rungs_q256 renamed attested_rungs_q256 because it never was the decodable set and reading it as one is how the gap opened: it is the rungs a lane_eligibility cell attests. Added an explicit grid to each entry so a (route, grid) pair with no published range refuses rather than resolving to another entry's numbers. candidate_rungs_q256 is retained as a DEPRECATED ALIAS of attested_rungs_q256 -- same list, refused if it disagrees -- so this stays an ADDITIVE change that a v1 reader can still read, which is why the schema string does not move. It is dropped at schema v2.
First published contract: two dense families, four cells, TP1/EP0.
